THIS MFA IS FILED U/S. 173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO ALLOW THIS APPEAL AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION TO RS. 12,99,008/- (EXCLUDING THE AMOUNT AWARDED BY THE TRIBUNAL) ALONG WITH INTEREST BY MODIFYING THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT-VIII AT MUDDEBIHAL DATED 25.02.2019 IN MVC NO.
70/2012.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)
Captioned appeal is by widow and minor son of deceased, questioning the quantum determined by Tribunal in MVC No.70/2012.
Claimants herein filed a claim petition for having lost one Sharanappa in a road traffic accident dated 02.02.2012.
Claimants contended that deceased was engaged in agriculture business and was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.

Tribunal in absence of income proof, notionally assessed income of deceased at Rs.5,730/- and without adding future prospects, awarded NC: 2024:KHC-K:9552 a sum of Rs.7,79,280/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Tribunal in all awarded a sum of Rs.11,60,992/-.

2. Heard learned counsel for appellants and learned standing counsel for Insurance Company.
3.
Tribunal having assessed the documents produced by claimants, refused to accede to the claim made by appellants that deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Therefore, Tribunal notionally assessed the income of deceased at Rs.5,730/-.
Though, this Court has re-assessed the material on record, this Court more particularly has taken note of RTC extracts produced at Ex.P8 to P13.

As on the date of accident, RTC extracts reveal that land held by deceased was subjected to cultivation and crops were grown and after his death, RTC extracts clearly reveal that no crops are grown.
4. These significant details reflected in RTCs, give rise to presumption that widow of deceased, after his NC: 2024:KHC-K:9552 death, is not in a position to cultivate the land in question.

However, in absence of income proof, this Court is not inclined to accede to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for Insurance company that income may be determined as per income chart prepared by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
As per income chart, income of deceased works out to Rs.6,500/-.
But, this income chart relates to agricultural coolies, labourers, workers, etc., whose income proof is not available.

In the case on hand, deceased owned the agricultural land and there is Akkamadevi W/O Sharanappa Bisanal And ... vs Mr. Prabhuraj S/O Venkanagouda And Anr on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44016211/
2 evidence that he used to cultivate the said land.
Therefore, owner of land cannot be equated to agricultural coolie.
However, by taking Rs.6,500/- as bench mark and having regard to RTC extracts, this Court notionally assesses the income of deceased at Rs.8,000/-.

After adding 40%
towards future prospects, income of deceased works out to Rs.11,200/-.

After deducting 1/3rd,
income works out to Rs.7466.66/-.

Compensation under the head of loss of dependency works out to Rs.15,23,199/-
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9552 (7466.66 x 12 x 17), which is rounded off to Rs.15,23,200/-.
5.

Under conventional heads, appellants are entitled for a compensation of Rs.1,10,000/-, along with additional 20% escalation Rs.22,000/- as per law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi1.
